text:
Two teams sliding meet in Winnipeg, and both are 1-4-0 in their last five. Vancouver (VAN) has lost three straight despite taking 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its last game, a 5-4 home loss to Anaheim in which Cutter Gauthier scored three goals, and it's missing Filip Chytil. Winnipeg (WPG) just snapped a nine-game winless run by coming back from four goals down to beat Montreal 5-4 in overtime, without Josh Morrissey and Vladislav Namestnikov. Luke Schenn also returns to Winnipeg for the first time since leaving the Jets.

Our numbers lean Winnipeg, 3.42 expected goals to 2.95. At five on five, WPG has controlled 46% of the chances to VAN's 41%, and Vancouver gives up 3.83 expected goals per 60 minutes. Vancouver also takes 4.2 penalties a game. Winnipeg's power play is the more dangerous one. In net, projected starters Leevi Meriläinen (VAN, +0.77 goals saved above expected this season, -17.93 last) and Stuart Skinner (WPG, +1.42 this season, +5.96 last) have both been steadier this year than Meriläinen was last.

Kyle Connor leads our picks at 49% to score and 78% for a point, with Mark Scheifele at 38%, still looking for a goal after eight games on 3.6 expected goals. For Vancouver, Jake DeBrusk (29%) works the top power play, and Filip Hronek is a point from 300 for his career. Our under-the-radar picks: Cole Perfetti (WPG), 55% for a point because his line creates chances and Vancouver allows the second-most expected goals per 60, and Linus Karlsson (VAN), a third-liner with 2.5 expected goals in his last 10 games.
